findings.title: Routing rollup asserts no quality loss without quality evidence
findings.what: The provenance inference says turns classified from prompt/tool/edit/output footprint can be routed to a cheaper tier “without quality loss.” The observations at lines 95-108 cite only the heuristic classification and cost extrapolation; neither is an outcome comparison or quality measurement. This converts a capability heuristic into an unsupported quality guarantee.
findings.fix: Remove the “without quality loss” guarantee and describe routing as a low-confidence candidate requiring replay/evaluation, or require and cite outcome-quality evidence before emitting that claim.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with footprint-only routing evidence produces wording that explicitly requires quality validation and contains no quality guarantee; a separate fixture may use stronger wording only when structured quality-result provenance is present.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read lines 61-115. The only observations cite computeModelRecommendations/summarizeModelRecommendations and estimateMonthlySavings; no cited field measures correctness, retries, user acceptance, or another quality outcome.

findings.title: Output-verbosity evidence can overstate the prose tokens used in its calculation
findings.what: Per session, proseTokens is correctly capped at totalOutput for savings, but proseChars accumulates the original uncapped textLength. Evidence and provenance later report proseChars/4 as prose output tokens. If parsed text length exceeds billed output×4, the card reports more prose tokens than were used for savings and potentially more than total billed output.
findings.fix: Accumulate the capped proseTokens value for displayed evidence/provenance instead of raw textLength, and use that same accumulator for both claims and arithmetic.
findings.acceptance: Given textLength/4 greater than totalOutput, emitted prose-token evidence is at most totalOutput, equals the token basis used for compression, and the provenance value/claim remains arithmetically consistent.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the split basis: line 92 computes the capped value, line 96 uses it for savings, while line 105 stores uncapped characters and lines 163 and 172 convert those uncapped characters back to tokens.

findings.title: Three cost detectors emit recommendation claims without structured provenance
findings.what: These returned recommendations omit provenance entirely. Their claims therefore do not identify reproducible source fields for priority-session counts and premium status, unknown-model fallback pricing, or web-search request counts/rates/spend share. Short session IDs in evidence do not establish the calculation inputs or pricing source.
findings.fix: Add provenance observations naming the exact tokenData entry/session fields and pricing-registry fields used, separate recommendation inference from observations, and include an as-of value/stale handling where timestamps are available.
findings.acceptance: For each detector, a representative emitted recommendation passes the repository provenance validator and exposes observations whose field/value entries reproduce its affected count and every numeric cost/share claim; stale historical inputs are dated or demoted.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read each complete return object and its immediately preceding calculation. None contains a provenance property. The comparison implementation model-eval-routing-gap.ts was not included in findings and only confirmed that structured observations/inference/asOf are representable by the detector type.
